content:
Before the official launch of macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple continues its weekly beta releases, and the company is now rolling out beta 8 to developers. Here's what everyone can expect.

Update: 5:04 PM ET — Public beta users can now download it.

macOS 27 beta 8 is now available

Developers can now install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 8, as Apple continues its preparations for the official release of this operating system in the coming weeks.

While macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7 didn't include any notable user interface changes, beta 6 introduced redesigned red, yellow, and green window control buttons with a look that more closely fits the Liquid Glass aesthetic.

At this stage of the beta cycle, Apple appears to be increasingly focused on bug fixes, performance improvements, and other behind-the-scenes tweaks ahead of the public release of macOS 27.

macOS 27 Golden Gate brings a brand new Siri app, complete with Apple's significantly revamped Siri AI, as well as an AI-powered Shortcuts app that can create shortcuts based on natural language commands. Safari also gains an instruction-based extensions builder.

Other updates include new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, along with the return of fixed-radius rounded corners for windows and apps, following the dynamically changing rounded corners introduced in macOS 26.

We're testing macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 8 in depth and will report back if we find anything new.

How to install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 8:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the 'i' icon next to Beta Updates
  • From the dropdown menu in the top right corner, select 'macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta'
  • Click Done

Have you found any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments.
